cards.title: One round registry + shared settle core: next audio round is a row, not 5 forks
acceptance: case 1: roundOf('AU2'|'AU2b'|'AU3') from rounds.json -> exactly {cap:5000,floor:14000,minReserve:8000,dir:'r2'}, {cap:3000,floor:13000,minReserve:8000,dir:'r3'}, {cap:10000,floor:1000,minReserve:1000,dir:'r4'} (pins today's hard-coded ceilings; no loosening)

cards.rollback: Three commits: (1) registry, settle module and tests; (2) elevenlabs/run-r4 switched to them; (3) dispatchers read the registry. Each reverts on its own, and the guard tests are the proof at every step.
cards.runner_up: Fold the build-r2/r3/r4 shared HTML helpers (table/header/player/footer, copied 3x) into one report_kit.py.
cards.body:
## Summary
Every authorized audio round so far has copied the guard, launcher, builder, checker and evidence script and added another `if wave==` branch. This card moves the per-round facts into one registry and the money-moving postflight into one module. The next owner-authorized round then needs one reviewed registry row.

## Description
`rounds.json` holds, per wave: cap ceiling, account floor, minimum reserve, output dir, plan file, launcher kind (brief|composition), music duration ceiling, and builder/checker module names. `elevenlabs.mjs` `budget()` reads its ceilings from it and keeps the same refusal message. The output-dir ternary and the dispatcher if-chains become lookups. `settle.mjs` exports the pure postflight transaction: the settlement-read schedule, the observed delta (reset-aware for AU3), `chargedCredits = max(...)`, and the flags. Both `generate()` and `run-r4.mjs` call it. Historical rounds keep their scripts; only how a script is chosen changes. The registry may never raise a ceiling. Case 1 pins today's values, so raising one is a policy change.

## Flow
- Add rounds.json, settle.mjs and rounds.test.mjs, with cases 1-6 failing first.
- Switch budget(), the output dir and the AU2b plan gate to roundOf(); switch both postflights to settle().
- Switch the build-reports.py and check-reports.py dispatch to the registry.
- Add the new files to the guard fixtures' copy lists and run the 28 guard tests unchanged.

## Expected impact
Opening a new round touches 1 registry row plus its plan, instead of about 5 new scripts and 4 edited branches. The two copies of the charge math can no longer drift. The proof needs no paid call.

## Evaluation
Claim: one registry plus one settle module removes the per-round forks with identical guard behavior.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass. rounds.json and settle.mjs do not exist, so cases 1-6 fail on import. Case 7 is green today and must stay green.
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - node --test tools/audio/*.test.mjs (offline, fetch intercepted, fake key)
Result: better
Gate: architecture

'r3' : 'r2';`; run-r4.mjs:71 `entry.chargedCredits=Math.max(estimate,entry.accountDelta??0,entry.settledDelta??0,entry.measuredCredits??0);` vs elevenlabs.mjs:188 `accountCost(observedDelta, upper, measured)`. build-reports.py has 3 wave branches and check-reports.py has 2. Baseline: node --test guard.test.mjs guard-r4.test.mjs -> tests 28, pass 28, fail 0 (run 2026-10-25 at 2d83a1e).

cards.body:
## Summary
The owner's listening verdicts are the scarcest input in this pipeline, and rounds 3 and 4 are still waiting for them. A verdict takes five manual steps to reach the repo: pick in a browser, copy, paste into prose, have an agent re-read the prose, hand-copy it into a PICKS dict. This card makes a verdict a record. It ingests the Markdown the page already exports, keeps an append-only choices.json, and gives the operator a status board of what is still pending.

## Description
`node tools/audio/choices.mjs ingest <file|->` parses the format report.js already exports. The title line gives the round; each row gives label | pick | samples | note, with escapeCell reversed. It checks every sample id against ledger.jsonl and the round's references, then merges into docs/audio/choices.json idempotently, keeping a history of revisions. `choices.mjs status` reads the data-direction cards on each audition page and prints, per round, which cards are pending, picked or kept. `choices.mjs kept` lists the sample ids whose latest pick is keep, with their round. `choices.mjs render <round>` regenerates the CHOICES.md table from the data. choices.json starts from the round-1 table, which parses exactly. Round 2 exists only as prose and the builder does not transcribe it; status marks it 'verdicts recorded as prose only'. The report.js copy message names the ingest command. No verdict is invented: only rows the owner exported get in.

## Flow
- Owner triages r3/r4 in the browser -> Copy Markdown -> `node tools/audio/choices.mjs ingest -` (paste) -> done.
- `choices.mjs status` -> 'r3 10/10 pending, r4 17/18 pending, r2 prose-only'.
- `choices.mjs kept` -> the derived keep list, which the AU4 importer can be checked against.

## Expected impact
The verdict hand-off goes from 5 manual steps to 1 command. Pending owner work becomes visible: 28 cards are unjudged today. The pick list for shipped audio gets a source it can be diffed against instead of being maintained by hand.

## Evaluation
Claim: verdicts round-trip without loss from the existing export into structured data, and pending work can be computed from the pages.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass (choices.mjs does not exist)
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - node --test tools/audio/*.test.mjs (pure parsing over fixtures plus the repo's CHOICES.md and pages, no network)
Result: better
Gate: direction
